result.summary: Wraps CWallet::CreateNew in a try-catch block in CreateWallet to catch std::runtime_error during wallet setup, such as external signer failures. When wallet creation fails, it removes newly created database files and directories using non-throwing filesystem calls while leaving pre-existing files and symlinks intact. It also updates the RPC error response from RPC_MISC_ERROR (-1) to RPC_WALLET_ERROR (-4).
result.problem: Setting up an external-signer wallet throws std::runtime_error if the signer fails or returns an invalid descriptor. In bitcoin-qt, this uncaught exception on a worker thread triggers std::terminate and crashes the application. In both GUI and RPC, failed creation leaves behind an empty wallet directory and wallet.dat, causing subsequent creation attempts with the same name to fail with 'Database already exists'.
evidence: Author provides reproduction steps on master showing `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'` and aborting bitcoin-qt when an invalid signer is used (PR description).
References bitcoin-core/gui#395 where this uncaught exception was previously encountered (PR description).
result.changed_since_previous: Added a release note in doc/release-notes-36767.md; the code changes and test coverage remain the same.
result.card: Catches std::runtime_error in CreateWallet so external signer setup failures display an error dialog instead of aborting bitcoin-qt via std::terminate. It also cleans up newly created wallet files and directories upon failed wallet creation, allowing users to immediately retry with the same wallet name rather than failing with 'Database already exists'. Over RPC, failed signer setup now returns RPC_WALLET_ERROR (-4) instead of an unhandled exception error (-1).

risk.why: A flaw in the file cleanup logic after a failed wallet creation could unintentionally remove pre-existing user files, directories, or symlink targets.
